# Tier B allowlist for .github/deadcode.sh — functions with NO PRODUCTION CALLER
# on linux, windows AND darwin. Each one is reachable only from its own tests.
#
# ONE LINE PER FUNCTION, as `<import path>.<func>`. Keyed on the name, never on
# file:line — a line number churns on every edit above it, which would make this
# file go stale for reasons that have nothing to do with reachability.
#
# 🔴 THIS FILE IS A DEBT LEDGER, NOT AN EXEMPTION LIST. Same discipline as
# contrast_web_test.go's 25 accepted light-theme debt entries: the set is
# ASSERTED, so the gate fails when it GROWS (something new became
# production-unreachable) and equally when it SHRINKS (an entry is no longer
# dead — delete the line and take the win). Adding a line to turn a red build
# green is a last resort, and the commit message has to say why it must stay.
#
# ⚠ THIS HEADER USED TO SAY "these 15 were MEASURED, not investigated" and that
# no entry had been checked. That sweep is DONE. All 15 were investigated; 14 are
# resolved and the one that remains carries its reason below.
#
#   - 12 were SUPERSEDED WRAPPERS, not dropped features: a no-argument form of a
#     function whose explicit-argument sibling is what production calls
#     (galleryTile/galleryTileW, startRun/startRunWithMessage,
#     parseWidgetOverrides/…ForModes, runModesPanel/…Selected,
#     runParamField/…Value, tileThumbWidth/…W, comfy.IsWidget vs the method,
#     RegistryClient.LookupClass{,es} vs LookupClassRaw + NodePackResolver, and
#     civitai.DecodeImageSearch vs DecodeLeveledImageSearch). All deleted, with
#     `go build ./...` at exit 0 as the proof and every test repointed at the LIVE
#     entry point — including the three LookupClasses tests, which now pin the
#     concurrency cap / determinism / blank-class properties on RegistryPacks.
#   - 2 (web.runParametersPanel, web.implicitPresetView) were genuine test
#     scaffolding sitting in production files. They moved to
#     internal/web/run_implicit_view_test.go, where the tier-B analysis (which
#     never loads test files) correctly stops seeing them — with
#     TestImplicitPresetViewMatchesTheProductionNoPresetView + its positive
#     control pinning them against the production builder so the "second parallel
#     renderer" risk cannot go quiet.
#
# The one KEPT entry, and why it must stay:
#
#   queue.Worker.ProcessOne — the only way to advance the download queue by
#   EXACTLY one item. ~22 call sites across internal/queue and
#   internal/integration depend on that to assert per-item state between steps.
#   Production genuinely has no single-step caller (Run loops; `check --download`
#   and the backfills go through DrainAll / DrainSubscription / DrainItems), and
#   DrainAll is not a substitute for the tests — it calls RequeueInterrupted and
#   then drains to empty, destroying the intermediate states they observe. The
#   function's own doc comment now says this; it previously claimed a
#   "one-shot `check` path" caller that does not exist.
#
# What this sweep did NOT cover, so nobody reads a short ledger as "everything
# runs": deadcode proves unreachable-from-a-root only. It cannot see a REACHABLE
# function behind a condition the app never satisfies, a fixture that picks the
# wrong branch, or a registered route nothing links to (that last one has its own
# guard, TestEveryRegisteredRouteIsEmitted). It also reports only FUNCTIONS —
# store.NodePackSourceExtensionNodeMap, for instance, is an exported const with no
# production reader, mirroring a key internal/comfy owns, and no tier reports it.
#
# Regenerate with:  .github/deadcode.sh --print

github.com/ZacxDev/civitai-manager/internal/queue.Worker.ProcessOne
